title: Turkana Research Project
content:
Turkana Research Project compiles information about the biocultural projects that the , of the University of Helsinki, leads in and around Sibiloi National Park. Sibiloi is the most remote park in Kenya. Well known for the hominid fossil discoveries, the area is considered as the most probable location for the origins of the human species.

Yet the biodiversity of Sibiloi has remained unexplored and unattended. Concerns about large infrastructure development have put more eyes in the area, which appears now to be largely defaunated. The magnitude of this defaunation is unknown. And so are the recovery prospects. Sibiloi and  surroundings are the home of three pastoralist groups, the Daasanach, the Gabra and the Turkana, that although originally adapted to live in this extreme and variable conditions, are now struggling due to several socio-political and environmental pressures. These groups have long had close relationship with the flora and the fauna, but this relationship is also changing.

title: New course: Principles of High-Throughput Plant Phenotyping
content:
This course provides a practical and research-oriented introduction to modern high-throughput plant phenotyping. Students learn how digital imaging, sensor technologies, robotics and data analytics are used to measure plant traits efficiently across controlled and field environments. The course combines online teaching with an intensive in-person training week at NMBU and UiO.

When: 22 September – 9 October 2026
Where: NMBU, UiO and online
Credits: 5 ECTS (BIO412)

  • Core principles of plant phenotyping and biological imaging
  • Introduction to field phenotyping
  • Controlled-environment phenotyping using advanced imaging systems
  • High-throughput seed phenotyping and trait-based sorting for model and crop species
  • Image processing, machine learning and data-analysis pipelines
  • Designing phenotyping experiments and handling large datasets

    • PhD students in plant sciences, biology, biotechnology, environmental sciences or related fields. MSc students may be admitted if space allows.

    Online sessions (20 h total):

  • 22 September, 13:00–17:00
  • 25 September, 12:00–16:00
  • 29 September, 13:00–17:00
  • 2 October, 12:00–16:00

    • In-person week (5–9 October, approx. 40 h):

  • 2 days at NMBU
  • 2 days at UiO
  • 1 day for student presentations

title: Online Lecture Series 2026: Hospicing Education? Reflexive and Critical Approaches to Education and Research
content:
Inspired by ongoing conversations around hospicing modernity, the series creates space for critical and reflexive inquiry into assumptions that shape contemporary education and educational research. Across seven online lectures, researchers and scholars engage with questions related to education development, modernity, educational reform, remote teaching and educational equity, competition, participatory research, decolonial approaches and climate justice.

All lectures are held online.

title: HSSH August Newsletter 8/2026
content:
The seventh edition of the Academic Career Planning and Leadership course (ACLA) is now open for applicants (deadline 10.9.2026 at 15:00). This course is targeted to post-doctoral researchers who are launching their independent research careers and are thinking about building their own research group. 

We will discuss career planning and trajectories, strategic mapping of research horizons, funding opportunities and challenges, building and leading a research group, project management, social impact issues and publication strategies, data management, and research ethics.

.

Approximately 15–20 participants will be enrolled, representing a wide disciplinary range of social sciences and humanities across all faculties of the City Centre Campus. 

The course will convene in six sessions (Fridays, 10 –15) over the academic year. Workshop days are: October 9 (warm-up session), October 23, November 20, December 11, January 22, February 19, March 19, and April 16. 

Participants should make sure that they are able to commit to these dates. 

For early May 2027, we are planning an excursion to Brussels to learn about European science policy and funding opportunities.

title: Renewing intellectual history in the age of AI
content:
In 2026, Helsinki Computational History Group is entering a new phase. Over the previous decade, COMHIS helped establish bibliographic data science, integrated workflows for historical newspapers, large-scale text-reuse research and computational studies of publishing and public discourse. That accumulated interdisciplinary work now supports a closer connection between intellectual-historical questions, AI development and production computing.

The change is practical as well as conceptual. New language and vision models can be tested against historical collections on CSC’s computing infrastructure, and results can arrive quickly enough to alter the live research design. A failed image crop, a misleading semantic match or a book-specific layout convention is no longer merely cleaned away at the end: it can become the reason to revise the data, model, validation rule or historical question.

title: Shayan Gharib väittelee aiheesta Oppiminen datasiirtymän yhteydessä: jakaumien invarianssista rakenteelliseen mukautumiseen
content:
M.Sc. Shayan Gharib defends his PhD thesis “Learning under Data Shift: From Distributional Invariance to Structural Adaptation” on Friday the 11th of September 2026 at 13 in the University of Helsinki Main Building, Hall F3017 (Fabianinkatu 33, 3rd floor). His opponent is Associate Professor Jenni Raitoharju (University of Jyväskylä) and custos Professor Arto Klami (University of Helsinki). The defence will be held in English.

The thesis of Shayan Gharib is a part of research done in the Department of Computer Science and in the Multi-source Probabilistic Inference group at the University of Helsinki. His supervisor has been Professor Arto Klami (University of Helsinki).

title: Opettajankoulutusfoorumi juhli 10-vuotista taivaltaan
content: Teacher Education Forum has made a variety of achievements during its existence. Visioning the future of the Finnish teacher education and concretizing the plans in broad collaboration is an established way of working together in the Forum. In the Anniversary Seminar Forum’s current and future work were demonstrated. In her opening speech, President of the forum Professor Auli Toom considered the research, practice and accountability turns evolved in enactment and development of teacher education in Finland, and how they have been realized in the Finnish Teacher Education Forum as well. to the seminar and elaborated on the forum’s achievements and impact from a variety of perspectives. Dean Dr. Tiina Silander reflected on the significance of forum’s continuing work for the best of the Finnish teacher education and educational system.
